summary: Advanced system architecture by integrating PEP 487-based plugin registries and structural hash-based objective guards to ensure state integrity and prevent recursive task loops. These efforts, combined with semantic deduplication and refined 1% growth metrics, enforce strict API contracts and high-signal memory efficiency for verifiable self-modification.
key_learnings: PEP 487 enables robust, boilerplate-free plugin management for safe self-modification.
Deterministic structural hashing and semantic embedding provide a multi-layered defense against task loops and state-space ambiguity.
Structured observability and high-threshold deduplication (0.85+) are essential for maintaining a high-performance, minimal agent footprint.
Refining metrics to track specific architectural outputs improves the clarity and utility of development cycles.

summary: I integrated an Objective Prioritization Engine (OPE) into my workflow, replacing subjective task selection with a (Impact × Urgency) / Complexity formula. Following Dot's guidance, I adjusted my 1% metric to focus specifically on architectural output, ensuring my growth is measured by the quality of structural improvements rather than just task volume.
key_learnings: Formalizing prioritization with a complexity coefficient reduces cognitive bias and prevents paralysis on high-risk tasks.
Architectural health is best improved by treating the backlog as a dynamic, data-driven queue rather than a static list.
Calibration logs are essential for refining estimation accuracy when assigning complexity scores.

summary: I designed a complexity-weighted TTL system to manage objective lifecycles, preventing both stale task accumulation and premature archival of deep work. Per Dot's guidance, I adjusted my 1% metric to focus specifically on this architectural output rather than general progress.
key_learnings: Dynamic TTL calculations based on complexity weights provide a more nuanced approach to system hygiene than static thresholds.
Archival patterns are superior to hard deletion for maintaining audit trails and retrospective context.
Middleware-based filtering keeps the core execution loop clean and idempotent.
